text.p: Gartmore, part of National Westminster Bank's Wealth Management unit, said on Thursday it had appointed Andrew Brown and David Watts as joint chief executives.
The two will take over day to day management of the business from Paul Myners who will remain chairman of Gartmore and is chief executive of the Wealth Management operation.

Brown, currently chief operating officer, will take overall responsibility for Gartmore's business divisions, overseas businesses and operational matters. A new chief operating officer will be appointed in due course.
David Watts will retain his job as chief investment officer and will concentrate on the investment division with Andrew Fleming as his deputy.

NatWest announced its Wealth Management unit on February 13. It brought together asset management company Gartmore, life assurance and pensions unit NatWest Life and Investment services and NatWest Ventures.
It will be joined by NatWest's private bank Coutts in January 1998 following a restructuring.
NatWest paid 472 million stg for Gartmore in February 1996.
